correctness.rationale: Starting from the classical rectangular determinantal degree product, direct adjacent cancellation yields the stated exact rational curvature ratio. Dividing by m^4 gives the bulk limit R_lambda(x). The logarithmic derivative in lambda is strictly negative for lambda>1 and x in (0,1). At lambda*=(1+sqrt(17))/4, the difference between denominator and numerator factors exactly as the square of the displayed quadratic divided by 1088; that quadratic has exactly one root in (0,1). Monotonicity then gives the sharp two-sided aspect-ratio phase transition. A fresh exact symbolic reconstruction independently verified the adjacent ratio at an additional parameter point and the critical Q(sqrt(17)) square identity.
residual_risks: The asymptotic phase statement is only for bulk coranks c/m->x in (0,1); endpoint scalings are not covered.

originality.rationale: Friedland-Krattenthaler's complete 31-page primary paper was read through its introduction, parity sections, plane-partition section, and conclusions. It records the Harris-Tu rectangular degree product as formula (1.2) and studies parity/2-adic valuations and real matrix subspaces, not adjacent-rank log curvature or an aspect-ratio phase threshold. A current published square-matrix finding gives the lambda=1 special case and a Pell equality law, while the assigned result treats the genuinely rectangular two-parameter family and identifies the new global boundary lambda*=(1+sqrt(17))/4 separating persistent bulk log-convexity from uniform bulk log-concavity. Current Resultary search found no earlier rectangular threshold theorem.
